A game heavily based on the Kingdom series, but in my opinion too heavily while it leaves some QoL features behind. Challenging to beat, but it has no missable achievements. [b]Approximate amount of time to 100%:[/b] I guess around 10h or so [b]Estimated achievement difficulty:[/b] 6/10 [b]Minimum number of playthroughs needed:[/b] Multiple times, if you die in a scenario you have to start over that scenario from the very beginning [b]Is there a good guide available:[/b] No [b]Multiplayer achievements:[/b] No, but I expected that this game is easier in co-op mode [b]Missable achievements:[/b] No [b]Grinding Achievements:[/b] No [b]DLC-Only achievements:[/b] No [b]Speedrun achievements:[/b] No [b]Time-gated achievements:[/b] No [b]RNG-achievements:[/b] No [b]Does difficulty affect achievements:[/b] No [b]Unobtainable/glitched achievements:[/b] No Monarchy is a lot like the Kingdom series, you are a ruler on a horse who doesn't fight but has people who fight for you. You have archers and builders to build up your domain and defend it during the raids that happen at night time. Just like the Kingdom series it doesn't explain much about the game mechanics and it comes down to exploring a lot yourself. This isn't my favorite part in the Kingdom series either, but there you have the internet full of info and tips. However, Monarchy doesn't have that yet. It is also a lot harder than the Kingdoms series, especially with the die = restart. In the Kingdoms series, you get referred back to a previous island and don't lose it all, just parts of it. Before I started playing this I had a some doubt. It looked way too similar to the Kingdom series, but I love that series and would welcome more games like that. So I was wondering how much it would feel the same. And there are small things different, like the limit on how much buildings you build and the objectives of the scenarios, but it also is so similar. Including having archers and builders, and later on swordsman. I would even say that the costs for doing most things are quite similar. One coin to destroy a tree, having your archers hunt on animals for coins. Sadly for me this game felt like it left behind some of the nice mechanics that make Kingdom: Two Crowns and Kingdom 80's great but doesn't add much to take it in a different direction. Most of the achievements are quite easy and you'll unlock while playing through the game. the most challenging ones will be to complete all the scenarios as they are very challenging. None of them are missable. I give Monarchy 2,5 out of 5 stars. Except for a cartoonish art, this game doesn’t bring any innovation. The influence is obvious right away, so you will not have to figure out the mechanics if you have played a similar game before. None of this has changed. The purpose of the game is to travel left and right with your king or queen, spend cash wisely, and build structures to survive attacking armies. Each game begins with a tent, which serves as your base. After construction, a few icons representing other constructions will jump out. Each construction consumes one icon, so you can not construct everything you want. Upgrading the base tent will grant you more icons, although you rarely need more than one sort of building throughout your kingdom. The lone exception is walls, which allow you to expand. To construct a structure, you must first have an empty plot of ground on which to place whatever you wish. Expanding your kingdom and cutting down trees creates a plot of land. Of course, you must invest the appropriate amount of coins. Once a building is completed, you will need to invest further coins to create a soldier, worker, or farmer. New people for your empire are discovered in the wild or they’ll come to beg near the tent. They will not arrive for free, so you will need to invest additional coins. However, there is also a trader that arrives at the beginning of each day. He can deliver a chest of coins or new people, but the choice is yours. But you must save at least one coin for the trader, as he does not deliver for free. Your monarch is unable to fight, so he or she requires protection. You start with only one archer who follows you around, but that will not be enough. Your soldiers will roam about on their own and occasionally hunt animals for extra coins, but they are smart enough to shelter behind walls when enemies approach at night. Both enemies and your soldiers die after a single hit, so losing one can be costly. Sadly, the game manages to ruin a lot with bas design choices. One of the worst are enemy spawn points. If you manage to expand the kingdom with the enemy spawn inside it, you'll get attacked from within your kingdom. Your soldiers won't go clear out the enemy base, and you can't do anything alone. This makes everything pointless because enemies will simply swarm your soldiers from behind and kill everyone.

Steam Curator: https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36307721-Healthy-Criticism/ Monarchy is a 2D sidescroller, similar to the Kingdom series, as well as sons of Valhalla. It is considerably unintuitive, with no clear indication of what each scenario's goals are to achieve victory. It is very challenging, even on the easiest difficulty. The premise of the game is simple, but the execution is far from. You collect coin that you spend on cutting down trees, recruiting more villagers to convert into archers or builders, and you invest that coin into your infrastructure to produce more coin and improve your defences. The more trees you clear out, the more buildable land you unlock and your borders expand. That will additionally clear out the forest and let your horse run faster. The main gripe I have with the game is how challenging it can get. I would like to see the difficulty levels reflect their implied challenge spike a lot more accurately. Another thing I would also like to see is verbal descriptions of what each scenario presents the player as a challenge. Other than that, this is the general formula for this type of game. https://youtu.be/oEyXA_hkWU8

Full review: https://www.screenhype.co.uk/monarchy-review-a-fun-but-familiar-2d-strategy-adventure/ Monarchy is a decent 2D side-scrolling strategy game that combines base-building, resource management, and exploration with just the right amount of challenge. While the game’s game modes add variety, its lack of a story and clunky interface can be frustrating. That said, the freedom to shape your kingdom and the thrill of nightly survival make it addictively fun in short bursts.
